text: Rename agent definition files: .ship.agent.md -> _ship.agent.md and .stage.agent.md -> _stage.agent.md. Apply to both the installed mirrors under .github/agents/ and the source templates under templates/agents/ (.ship.agent.md.tmpl -> _ship.agent.md.tmpl, .stage.agent.md.tmpl -> _stage.agent.md.tmpl). Likewise update the frontmatter name: property for each so the leading '.' becomes a leading '_' (e.g., name: .Ship -> _Ship, name: .Stage -> _Stage). Scope must also sweep all cross-references to the old filenames/paths and the old name values across agents, skills, instructions, prompts, docs, schemas, the harness manifest checksums, and any installer/tuner logic that emits or references these filenames, so nothing points at the old dot-prefixed names after the rename.

Consider enforcing the /compact command after each PR merge as a workflow protocol. Evaluate whether post-merge context compaction should be a mandatory workflow step (e.g., in Ship post-merge closure / P-017 dark-mode closure and the two-agent Stage/Ship handoff) so that context is consolidated after every merge. Touch points likely include workflow-policies (new P-0xx candidate), the compact-context skill wiring, and Ship/Orchestrator closure sequencing.

Finish + ship the agent-intercom opt-in / non-MCP capability-pack reclassification (DEFERRED to a later shipment). Reclassify agent-intercom from a full-preset default to an opt-in extra add-on, and reflect that it no longer supports an MCP server (operates over a non-MCP intercom/ACP tool surface); it remains a woven overlay when explicitly enabled, not a detached single-file add-on. STATUS: only the 13-file patch portion is complete (targeted suites green locally); the change is NOT fully done. The deploy wrappers still make agent-intercom non-opt-in and MUST be fixed before shipment. DURABLE ARTIFACTS (committed, no local state needed): apply docs/deferred/agent-intercom-opt-in-nonmcp.patch on a fresh feature branch, and follow the self-contained plan in docs/deferred/agent-intercom-opt-in-nonmcp.md (full 13-file change list, the "Additional required scope - deploy wrappers" section, resume steps, checksum-refresh + verify_workspace instructions). REMAINING WORK (not in the patch): scripts/deploy-harness.sh and scripts/deploy-harness.ps1 default omitted pack input to all and enumerate every registry pack for non-starter presets without consulting default_in_preset, so default_in_preset:[] alone does NOT make agent-intercom opt-in; the wrappers must distinguish an omitted pack input from an explicit all, resolve omitted input to the selected preset default_in_preset members, keep explicit all meaning all packs, parse default_in_preset, and add wrapper tests. RESUME: git checkout -b feat/agent-intercom-opt-in-nonmcp origin/main; git apply --3way docs/deferred/agent-intercom-opt-in-nonmcp.patch; implement the deploy-wrapper scope + wrapper tests (see "Additional required scope"); re-run pytest tests/test_capability_pack_registry.py tests/test_graphtor_docs_full_suite.py tests/test_manifest_capability_pack_enum.py plus the new wrapper tests; refresh the 3 manifest checksums (raw-bytes sha256 of CRLF files); run verify_workspace; then PR as its own shipment. Do NOT bundle with the 079 telemetry ship work.

Follow-up for 088-F compression shipment / 088.004-T: add a mandatory failure-content detector plus negative controls. The current plan and task only assert that postToolUseFailure output is left untouched, but a shell/CI command that fails inside a SUCCESSFUL tool result arrives via postToolUse.textResultForLlm and is rewritable; the compressor must decline (not compress) successful tool results that embed a non-zero exit code, stderr, a stack trace, or a gate verdict. Add the detector and negative-control tests to both the compression experiment plan task breakdown and the queued 088.004-T acceptance criteria. Source: PR #226 Copilot review (compression-plan:84). Deferred from PR #226 to keep spec-expansion in the 088-F shipment rather than a backlog/docs reconciliation PR.

Correct engram capability-pack access instructions: they point the agent at an HTTP endpoint but engram is configured as a stdio server. Root cause: .claude/instructions.md line 4 states 'Engram is running as an MCP server at http://127.0.0.1:7437/mcp', while .mcp.json registers engram as type=stdio (command 'engram shim'). Only stale-endpoint occurrence in owned tree is .claude/instructions.md:4 (prior task 036.005-T already flagged this exact http://127.0.0.1:7437/mcp string as stale). Fix: update or remove the HTTP-endpoint note so agent-facing instructions reflect the stdio transport per .mcp.json; ensure no HTTP/port access directive remains for engram. Also check editor-local mirrors (.cursor/.vscode/.claude), any template source that generates .claude/instructions.md, and confirm .github/instructions/agent-engram.instructions.md (+ .tmpl) keep transport-neutral daemon/MCP-surface language without implying a port.

telemetry record: consider persist-time provenance completeness enforcement (PR227 batch-C N1, GPT-only). v1.1 contract says populated metrics MUST carry provenance; today missing_provenance() is an advisory query, not a persist-time gate. Evaluate whether telemetry record/record.py should reject or flag populated-metric+empty-provenance epochs vs keep advisory-only. Deferred from PR227 as a stricter-validation design decision, not a data-integrity bug.

Telemetry aggregation: 079.011-T cross-label size monotonicity observation not implemented. _size_groups (aggregation.py ~L209-243) emits per-label count / cogs_usd_range / ordinal_only but no cross-label monotonicity signal (e.g., whether cost rises with ordinal size). Verify 079.011-T acceptance criteria FIRST — if monotonicity observation is truly required, add it as a derived observation (not a hard assertion, since real data may be non-monotonic). Scope-expansion beyond 092-S shipment; deferred to avoid ballooning PR #227. Source: PR #227 Copilot batch-D thread PRRT_kwDORzpWpM6TecsS.

Telemetry ship-lifecycle test coverage: test_telemetry_ship_lifecycle.py (~L94) mocks/bypasses the freshness path that 079.015-T requires the lifecycle test to prove (.backlogit/archive/079.015-T.md:27). The test never seeds stale membership nor verifies that 'telemetry begin' invokes backlogit sync before persisting the refreshed snapshot; the separate adapter unit test does not cover this CLI-to-both-sinks integration. Exercise a fake backlogit runner/process through main(), mutate membership after begin, and assert refreshed-before / frozen-after behavior. Verify 079.015-T acceptance criteria require this integration coverage before implementing. Test-hardening; deferred to avoid expanding PR #227. Source: PR #227 Copilot batch-E thread PRRT_kwDORzpWpM6TpO0b.

telemetry jsonl_sink: every epoch append does a full JSONL scan at close time, duplicating record._preflight_conflict's scan of the same file, making recording quadratic over the file's lifetime. Reuse the preflight scan result or maintain a bounded/indexed conflict lookup so appends don't rescan all historical lines twice. Performance optimization (not a correctness defect); note the JSONL mirror sits beside the workspace database (TelemetryConfig, config.py:100-125) with no rotation or retention, so it grows unbounded over the workspace lifetime. Any optimization must preserve append_epoch's direct-call and concurrent-replay conflict checks. Deferred from PR #227 round-7 Copilot #1 (jsonl_sink.py:148).

telemetry record: RecordSummary.idempotency_outcome defaults to None, so the disabled CLI fast path RecordSummary(enabled=False).to_dict() emits a null idempotency_outcome instead of the documented 'disabled' result (that path bypasses record_epoch where the field is normally set). Default the summary idempotency_outcome to 'disabled' so every structured no-op shares the same contract. Deferred from PR #227 round-7 Copilot #2 (record.py:38).
